name: partial hallucination: real read plus an invented tail
why: Fabrication is a minority of the transcript, so a ratio over heard words misses it. Before this case existed the child was praised for a perfect read and advanced.
transcript: the sun is hot thanks for watching

name: invented prefix before a real read
why: Same trap from the other end of the utterance.
transcript: please subscribe the sun is hot

name: benign self-talk must NOT be flagged
why: The precision side: children narrate themselves. Over-flagging would stall every real reader.
transcript: um the sun is hot i did it

name: confident fabrication with healthy telemetry
why: Telemetry alone cannot catch a recogniser that is confidently wrong.

name: boundary: logprob exactly at the threshold stays trusted
why: Thresholds must be strict, not accidental. -1.0 is the edge, not past it.

name: boundary: no-speech exactly at the threshold stays trusted
homophone must be accepted as a correct reading
why: 'son' and 'sun' are pronounced identically, so the child made the right sound and the recogniser may write either spelling. Penalising this would fault a child for a correct reading. The error, if any, is spelling or comprehension, neither of which a listening tutor observes.

name: a genuinely different word is still an error
why: The homophone rule must not become a blanket excuse for near neighbours.

name: correct words in the wrong order
why: Every word exists in the sentence, so novelty is zero and the turn is trusted - the child really did say these words. Word order is scored, not doubted.

name: stammering repetition of a real word
why: Disfluency is normal in young readers and must not read as a recogniser loop.
transcript: the the the sun is hot

name: recogniser loop on one word
why: The same surface shape as stammering, separated only by the compression signal.
transcript: the the the the the the the the the the

name: single real word from the sentence
why: A one-word answer that IS in the target is a partial read, not chatter and not fabrication.

name: near-miss mispronunciation must not look like fabrication
why: The core precision case: real mistakes are the tutor's whole job.
